clauses.reason: The approval says: "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved". It is a section 3 approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Household Goods Storage & Moving Trade, so its operative effect was the code's legal force. Under section 3(b) of the Act the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations, and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor; that force was the whole operative effect of an approval. The order states no period, condition, 'until' date, stay or provisional approval of its own, and no held record cancels, suspends, modifies under section 10(b) or supersedes the code before June 14, 1935 (see earlier_end_check). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (Pub. Res. No. 26, 74th Cong., 49 Stat. 375, approved June 14, 1935) provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval on June 14, 1935. Repeal of the power to approve codes and of the provisions enforcing them removed the legal force that the approval gave the code, so this clause ended on June 14, 1935; effective date confirmed. The three provisos that follow are treated as separate clauses. June 16, 1935, Title I's original two-year expiry, is not an end date: section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; it is recorded as a validity characterization (an approval made under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing), not as an end date, because the decision cancelled no approving order and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on May 27, 1935.

The first proviso says "the provisions of Article VII, Section 1, insofar as they prescribe a waiting period between the filing with the Administrative Boards and the effective date of revised price lists or revised terms and conditions of sale be and they are hereby stayed pending further order by the Administrator either within a period of sixty (60) days from the effective date of this Code or after the completion of a study of open price associations now being conducted by the National Recovery Administration". It stays a code provision, so it depends on the code. The words 'either within a period of sixty (60) days ... or after the completion of a study' tell when the Administrator was to act; the stay itself lasts until a further order, and no held record shows an order, so it has no own-terms end. Once the code's legal force was repealed there was nothing left to stay. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (Pub. Res. No. 26, 74th Cong., 49 Stat. 375, approved June 14, 1935) provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval on June 14, 1935. This clause ended on June 14, 1935; effective date confirmed. June 16, 1935, Title I's original two-year expiry, is not an end date: section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; it is recorded as a validity characterization (an approval made under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing), not as an end date, because the decision cancelled no approving order and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on May 27, 1935.

The second proviso says "it is understood that Article II, Section 1, taken in conjunction with Article II, Section 1 of the Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry, is interpreted to mean that the question to be considered at the public hearing to be held prior to June 15, 1934, is whether or not vehicles engaged in the transportation of used household goods or used office furniture and equipment are to be included wholly or partly in the Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry or wholly or partly under this Code". It states the reading of Article II, Section 1 and the question for the hearing; it depends on the code, states no period, and no held record shows the hearing held or the question resolved, so no earlier end is established. The resolution states no effective date other than its approval on June 14, 1935. The third proviso says "the provisions of Article II, Section 1(c) shall be stayed pending the public hearing to be held prior to June 15, 1934, and pending my further order". inventory_overrides.reason: The approval itself (Now, Therefore through 'it is hereby approved'); the machine inventory folded it with three provisos into one clause.
First proviso: the stay of the Article VII, Section 1 waiting period; separate command inside the machine's single paragraph.
Second proviso: the interpretive understanding about Article II, Section 1 and the hearing question; separate command inside the machine's single paragraph.
Third proviso: the stay of Article II, Section 1(c); separate command inside the machine's single paragraph.

research_rationale:
EO 6684-D (1934-04-19, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (registered grade mirror_transcription, not an original; 2478 characters). Identity: the census register lists it as 'Executive Order 6684-D—Code of Fair Competition for the Household Goods Storage & Moving Trade' dated 1934-04-19; the WPA 1944 list has '1934 Apr 19 p.575: Code of Fair Competition for the Household Goods Storage and Moving Trade conditionallyapproved. IX NRA Codes 349.'. Page check: the mirror page record with the same source sha256 is headed 'Executive Order 6684-D—Code of Fair Competition for the Household Goods Storage & Moving Trade', dated 1934-04-19, from a common-crawl capture of 2025-09-11T05:23:22Z, and its text_sha256 equals the held text's; the heading names this order's number and the date and subject agree with the text. Machine inventory corrected: it is one paragraph (742-2442) holding four distinct commands, split below. (1) The approval: "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved", the Code of Fair Competition for the Household Goods Storage & Moving Trade (title I, section 3(a)). (2) A stay of the waiting period in Article VII, Section 1 "pending further order by the Administrator either within a period of sixty (60) days from the effective date of this Code or after the completion of a study of open price associations". (3) An understanding about the question for the public hearing to be held before June 15, 1934. (4) A stay of Article II, Section 1(c) "pending the public hearing to be held prior to June 15, 1934, and pending my further order". None states a fixed end date: the sixty-day phrase and the hearing date are times by which the Administrator or the President was to act, and every stay waits on a further order, so none has an own-terms end before June 14, 1935. First end of every clause: S.J. Res. 113 section 2, June 14, 1935; no earlier end is held.

June 16, 1935 and May 27, 1935 are not ends (see the clause reason). Amendments, if any, would be later events, not ends. EO 6723 (May 26, 1934) suspends, until further orders, the provisions (other than child labor, maximum hours, minimum rates of pay and sections 7(a) and 10(b)) of codes of service trades that the Administrator later designates; no held designation names this code, and a suspension of trade-practice provisions would not by itself end the approval.","independent_command_check":"No clause is independent of the code. savings.reason: Acts done under the approved code before June 14, 1935, and any liability for violating it before that date, are accrued effects. The general savings statute of the time (not a held source) preserved liabilities already incurred under a repealed statute; that preservation does not keep the approval operative. Section 5 of the Act exempted from the antitrust laws "any code, agreement, or license approved, prescribed, or issued and in effect under this title" and complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days after; whatever exemption survives for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect. The proviso in section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 says the exemption "shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder" of two kinds (section 7(a) requirements, and prohibiting practices already unlawful); it names agreements, not codes, and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source continues this approval after June 14, 1935 and no held source shows a prosecution continued after that date.
